why: The QCELL outlet (31 mbar) saturates at about 2.0 K, below the lambda point. CoolProp's helium EOS stops at the lambda point and only extrapolates there. NIST TN1334 covers He-4 from 0.8 K, so it is valid in He II. HEPAK v3.4 remains the governing backend.

transcription_provenance.note: No copy of the TN1334 report is held in any GBOGEB repo or on the owner workstation (searched 2026-11-18). Re-verify the three values below against the report pages before promoting this file.

unit_correction.reason: P05V labels inlet A as 'h_J_per_mol: 11.78' and the saturation pair as J/kg. Neither label is consistent with the physics or with P05N.
unit_correction.inlet_A_unit: J/g, as tabulated in TN1334 and as P05N records it (h_J_g: 11.78). P05V's own conversion (x 4002.6 = 47150) also treats it as J/g.
unit_correction.saturation_unit: J/mol. As J/kg the latent heat would be 93.1 J/g; He-4 at 2 K is about 23 J/g. As J/mol it is 23.26 J/g.
unit_correction.flash_fraction_effect: None. P05V scaled all three enthalpies by the molar mass, so its x = 0.43643 is unchanged by this correction.

external_reference.title: Thermophysical Properties of Helium-4 from 0.8 to 1500 K with Pressures to 2000 MPa

qcell_saturation.source: NIST helium saturation table as cited by cryoplant P05V (table and page not recorded there)

same_reference_state_check.method: Carry the saturated vapour at 2.000 K up to 3.6 K with ideal-gas cp = 5.193 J/g/K, then compare with TN1334's own 3.6 K / 10 kPa vapour row (P05N).
